tasks.title: Add the audit event constant, the local scrub and the shared go-git push core used by archive and branch push
steps: Write TS-38-37 (property test of the scrub), TS-38-41, TS-38-51 and TS-38-52 and confirm they fail
In internal/audit/types.go add `const EventBranchPush = "hub.branch.push"` with a doc comment in the style of EventForgeIssueCreate

Create internal/workspace/branch_push_scrub.go with `scrubText(text, secret string) string`: replace each occurrence of a non-empty secret with `[redacted]`, remove URL userinfo using the pattern `(?i)([a-z][a-z0-9+.\-]*://)[^/\s?#]*@` replaced by `${1}`, repeat until the text stops changing, then cut to 1024 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary (re-run stability so scrub(scrub(x))==scrub(x)); do not import internal/forge or internal/carrypatch; add a helper `stripUserinfoURL(gitURL)` that strips userinfo for scheme URLs and returns scp-style addresses (git@host:path) unchanged

Create internal/workspace/push_core.go with one shared function `pushToOrigin(ctx context.Context, repoPath, gitURL string, auth transport.AuthMethod, refSpecs []config.RefSpec, force bool) error` that does git.PlainOpen, then repo.PushContext with PushOptions{RemoteName:"origin", RemoteURL: gitURL, Auth, RefSpecs, Force}; return the raw go-git error (including git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate) and a distinguishable open error type; expose it through a package-level var seam (e.g. `pushToOriginFn`) so tests can count/replace calls

Rewrite defaultArchiveOpenAndPushFn in internal/workspace/clone.go to call the shared core with refspec `refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*`, no deadline (context.Background()), mapping git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate to ErrAlreadyUpToDate; keep the three-argument ArchiveOpenAndPushFuncType signature unchanged
Run the existing archive and reclone tests untouched and confirm they pass
Run `make doc` if exported identifiers changed (only audit.EventBranchPush)
done_when: archive_test.go, reclone_test.go and every test replacing archiveOpenAndPushFn pass without modification

tasks.title: Mount the branch push route with access checks, body parsing, name decoding and workspace preconditions
steps: Write the listed tests using newTestEnv/doRequest/patAuth/userAuth/adminAuth/seedOrg/newRealHub/mintPAT/bindToken and confirm they fail

Create internal/workspace/branch_push.go with `handleBranchPush(db *sql.DB) echo.HandlerFunc`; mount `api.POST("/workspaces/:slug/branches/:name/push", handleBranchPush(db))` in RegisterRoutes (routes.go) without adding it to wsaccess.AllowBoundTokens

Handler order: apikit.GetAuthInfo nil -> 401; PAT without workspaces:write (isPAT/hasScope) -> respondError 403 `PAT requires workspaces:write scope to push branches` with no error_type, before any workspace lookup; then lookupWorkspaceForAuth(c, db, slug, auth, wsaccess.NeedWrite) which writes 404/403/500 itself

Decode the name: take the segment before the trailing `push` from c.Request().URL.EscapedPath() and apply url.PathUnescape exactly once (same approach as forge/write_labels.go lastSegment) so `a%2525b` yields `a%25b`

Parse the body: empty body (io.EOF) means force=false; otherwise decode into a struct with `Force *bool`-style handling so a non-object, invalid JSON or non-boolean force yields respondError 400 `invalid request body: ...`; unknown fields ignored; do this before the lock

Validate the name with gitcmd.ValidateRefName; on failure answer 404 via respondErrorWithType with type `branch_not_found` and message `branch_not_found: "<name>" is not a valid branch name: <rule>`; this runs after access and before the lock
Check ws.Status == active (400 `workspace is not active; push requires an active workspace`) and ws.CloneStatus == ready (400 `workspace clone is not ready; clone_status must be 'ready' to push`)
Leave the remainder of the handler as an explicit temporary 501 respondError that task 3 replaces; confirm an unescaped slash in the name matches no route (router 404)
done_when: the route is registered and every refusal listed in 38-REQ-2 and 38-REQ-3 answers as specified

tasks.title: Apply carry-patch and protected-branch refusals, take the workspace lock, resolve the branch and run the push
steps: Write the listed tests (local bare repository as origin over a plain path; seed workspace rows and a real trunk under defaultWorkspaceRoot/<slug>/trunk) and confirm they fail

Before the lock: on WorkspaceMode == carry_patch, integration branch = IntegrationBranch column or `deploy` when empty; equal name -> 400 type `integration_branch` with message `integration_branch: ...` saying hub builds this branch and it reaches the fork through REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH; then getPatchByBranch(db, slug, name) with status != 'deleted' -> 400 `patch_branch: ...` pointing to PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN

Before the lock: when force is true and ws.Branch is set and equals the name -> 400 `protected_branch: ...` in both modes; any database error in these decisions -> 500 (respondError with generic internal message, logged scrubbed)

Take the lock with wslock.TryLock(slug) without waiting; on failure answer respondErrorWithType 409 `another operation is running on this workspace; retry later` type `workspace_busy`; defer unlock so it is released on every path

Under the lock open the trunk (git.PlainOpen at filepath.Join(defaultWorkspaceRoot, slug, "trunk")); when force and ws.Branch is nil, read repo.Head().Name().Short(); equal name -> 400 `protected_branch`; unreadable HEAD -> 500

Resolve refs/heads/<name> with repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(name), true); missing -> 404 type `branch_not_found` message `branch_not_found: branch "<name>" does not exist in the workspace`; otherwise the hash is `sha`

Run the push through the shared core with a minimal outcome mapping (success -> pushed/forced, NoErrAlreadyUpToDate -> up_to_date) and answer 200 with branch, sha, remote `origin`, remote_url; refine in tasks 4 and 5
Replace the temporary 501 of task 2 with this flow
done_when: no refusal in 38-REQ-4 sends anything to the forge and the lock is free after each answer

tasks.title: Finish the successful push: credential resolution, refspec, result values, remote_url and body defaults
steps: Write the listed tests; for TS-38-29 build an HTTP stand-in forge (net/http/cgi with `git http-backend`, http.receivepack=true, wrapped by a recording handler) that records Authorization headers, refspecs/ref updates; confirm they fail
Resolve the credential with ResolveCloneAuth(secrets.NewStore(db), slug); on store error answer 500 `internal server error` and log it scrubbed, before contacting the forge

Build the refspec exactly `refs/heads/<name>:refs/heads/<name>`, or `+refs/heads/<name>:refs/heads/<name>` when force; pass Force only through the refspec plus the PushOptions.Force flag consistent with the shared core
Compute result: git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate -> up_to_date (even with force), force requested and push accepted -> forced, otherwise pushed
Set remote_url with stripUserinfoURL(ws.GitURL) (scheme URLs lose userinfo, scp-style unchanged); response uses `remote: origin`
Verify the percent-decode-once property (TS-38-2) against escaped names including `%25` sequences, and that empty/`{}`/unknown-field bodies push non-forced
done_when: a repeated push of an unchanged branch answers up_to_date and sends no objects

tasks.title: Map push failures to non_fast_forward and forge_* answers
steps: Write the listed tests using the HTTP stand-in forge and local bare origins (pre-receive hook for rejection, closed port and unresolvable host for unreachable) and confirm they fail

Add a `classifyPushError(err, credKind)` in branch_push.go checking errors.Is/As against git.ErrNonFastForwardUpdate, transport.ErrAuthenticationRequired, transport.ErrAuthorizationFailed, transport.ErrRepositoryNotFound, context.DeadlineExceeded and net errors (net.Error, DNS, x509/TLS), with a fallback on lowercased error text (`non-fast-forward`, `fetch first`, `401`, `403`, `not found`, `rejected`/`declined`/`hook`); statuses: 409 non_fast_forward, 502 forge_unauthenticated, 502 forge_forbidden, 404 forge_not_found, 422 forge_rejected, 504 forge_timeout, 502 forge_unreachable, 502 forge_error

For non_fast_forward list origin's refs once with git.NewRemote(memory.NewStorage(), &config.RemoteConfig{Name:"origin", URLs: gitURL}).ListContext with the same auth and same deadline context; if refs/heads/<name> is found name its commit; end with `push with force to overwrite it` unless the branch is the workspace's own branch (branch column, or HEAD branch read under the lock), in which case end with `sync the workspace to bring it up to date`; omit the commit when the listing fails

For forge_unauthenticated say whether the workspace has no stored credential or the forge rejected GIT_PAT or GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD (kind from the BasicAuth username `x-token-auth`), never the value; for forge_rejected carry the scrubbed forge reason
Every own-type message begins `<error_type>: `; messages are built from scrubText, never from the raw go-git chain
Distinguish hub-internal failures (trunk cannot be opened, no `origin` remote) from push attempts and answer them 500 without a push-attempt classification
done_when: origin's refs are listed exactly once per non-fast-forward refusal

tasks.title: Run the push detached with a two-minute deadline, emit the hub.branch.push event and log failures scrubbed
steps: Write the listed tests (capturing emitter via SetAuditDependencies/RegisterRoutesWithConfig as in handlers_audit_test.go, captured slog output, SSE broadcaster for TS-38-42) and confirm they fail

Run the push and the origin listing on `context.WithoutCancel(c.Request().Context())` wrapped in context.WithTimeout of a fixed 2-minute constant (overridable in tests through an unexported var only); a passed deadline maps to 504 forge_timeout; the caller disconnecting never cancels the push

On every push attempt (success, up_to_date, forced, 409, 404 forge_not_found, 422, 502s, 504) emit exactly one audit.EventBranchPush via emitHubAudit on a WithoutCancel context: ResourceType `branch`, ResourceID branch name, Action `push`, Workspace slug, Metadata branch, sha, force, ok, remote `origin`, remote_url (userinfo removed), plus result when ok or error_type when not; no credential or forge text; pass every value through scrubText
Log each failed push attempt exactly once at warning level with fields workspace, branch, error_type and error=scrubText(err, secret); log nothing under this rule on success
Log every 500 answer the way hub logs internal errors, scrubbed with the credential secret; ensure no refusal (401, 403, 404, 400, workspace_busy, any 500) emits an event
Audit all error message construction in branch_push.go so that the response never contains the credential secret, git_url userinfo or the raw go-git chain
done_when: no response body, audit event or log line contains the credential secret or git_url userinfo

tasks.title: Hold the lock until the push ends and restore the trunk worktree after a concurrent push to hub
steps: Write the listed tests (blocking push seam via the shared core var, a hook that advances refs/heads/main without touching the worktree, a failing-reset seam, captured log) and confirm they fail

Ensure the unlock is deferred in the handler goroutine and the handler does not return before the detached push has ended, so a disconnected caller still leaves the lock held until the push completes and the lock is released on every path

Right after taking the lock record the commit repo.Head() resolves to (ignore if unreadable); before releasing the lock re-read it; if both are known and differ, hard-reset the worktree via repo.Worktree().Reset(&git.ResetOptions{Commit: newHash, Mode: git.HardReset}) through an unexported seam so tests can make it fail
On a failed reset log exactly one warning (scrubbed, no secret) and leave the answer unchanged; if HEAD is unmoved or unreadable at either point leave the worktree untouched and log no reset warning
Confirm owner API key, scoped PAT, bound PAT on its own slug and admin token all answer 200 (TS-38-15)
done_when: TryLock on the slug succeeds after every answer and after a disconnected push ends
